The '''2015–16 season''' was '''[[FC Barcelona|Futbol Club Barcelona]]''''s 117th in existence and [[FC Barcelona|the club]]'s [[La Liga#Clubs|85th consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football. Barcelona was involved in six competitions after completing its second [[Treble (association football)|continental treble]] in the [[2014–15 FC Barcelona season|previous season]].

The season produced a [[Double (association football)#Spain|domestic double]] of La Liga and Copa del Rey wins, with Barça coming out on top in a closely fought title race and defeating newly crowned Europa League winners [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] in the Copa del Rey final after extra time. However, Barça failed to clinch its second [[Sextuple (football)|sextuple]] after 2009 by losing the Supercopa de España to Copa del Rey runners-up [[Athletic Bilbao]] (0–4 away, 1–1 home). Barcelona did manage to finish the year with five trophies, repeating 2011, by clinching the UEFA Super Cup and FIFA Club World Cup titles. Barcelona was also aiming and considered a favourite to repeat as Champions League winners to become the first team in the modern era to do so, but they were knocked out by [[Atlético Madrid]] in the quarter-finals (2–1 home, 0–2 away) in a strange repeat of their [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Quarter-finals|meeting at the same stage]] two years prior.

The season was the first since [[1997–98 FC Barcelona season|1997–98]] without former captain [[Xavi (footballer, born 1980)|Xavi]], who departed to [[Al Sadd SC]].

==Season overview==
===June===
On 7 June, Barcelona announced the transfer of [[Midfielder#Winger|right-wing]] [[Aleix Vidal]] from fellow [[La Liga]] outfit and [[2015 UEFA Europa League Final|2015 UEFA Europa League]] winners [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]]. The player will join on a five-year deal with a transfer fee of €18&nbsp;million plus variables.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/aleix-vidal-signs-up-till-2020 |title=Vidal joins Barça. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=7 June 2015 |access-date=8 June 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150609023647/http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/aleix-vidal-signs-up-till-2020 |archive-date=9 June 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On 9 June, the club announced that right back [[Dani Alves]] is set to stay at the club after signing a contract renewal for two years with an option for another year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/agreement-to-renew-dani-alves-contract |title=Agreement to renew Alves' contract. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=9 June 2015 |access-date=9 June 2015}}</ref> On 10 June, Barcelona announced that the presidential elections will take place on 18 July, after [[Josep Bartomeu]] resigned as president to qualify for re-election.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/club/detail/article/fc-barcelona-presidential-elections-on-18-july |title=Barça to vote for new President. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=10 June 2015 |access-date=11 June 2015}}</ref> On 25 June, Barcelona announced [[La Masia]] graduate [[Gerard Deulofeu]] was transferred to [[Premier League|English side]] [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] for a reported fee of €6&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/agreement-with-everton-fc-for-transfer-of-gerard-deulofeu |title=Deulofeu returns to Everton. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=25 June 2015 |access-date=25 June 2015}}</ref> The player returned to [[Merseyside]] after spending the [[2013–14 Everton F.C. season|2013–14 season]] on loan there under fellow Spaniard manager [[Roberto Martínez]].

===July===
On 3 July, Barcelona announced that La Masia graduate [[Martín Montoya]] would join [[Serie A|Italian side]] [[Inter Milan|Internazionale]] on a season-long loan with an option for a second.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/martin-montoya-joins-inter-milan-on-loan |title=Montoya joins Internazionale. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=3 July 2015 |access-date=6 July 2015}}</ref> On 6 July, Barcelona announced the signing of [[Turkey national football team|Turkey national team captain]] [[Arda Turan]] from [[Atlético Madrid]] for €34&nbsp;million. The player will join on 1 January 2016 after the [[FIFA]] transfer ban is lifted.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/agreement-with-atletico-madrid-for-the-signing-of-arda-turan |title=Arda completes move to Barça. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=6 July 2015 |access-date=6 July 2015}}</ref> On 18 July, Josep Bartomeu was elected president of Barcelona for the next six years with the third most votes in the club's history.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/club/detail/article/josep-maria-bartomeu-escollit-president-del-fc-barcelona |title=Bartomeu elected new president. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=18 July 2015 |access-date=21 July 2015}}</ref> On 21 July, Barcelona kicked off the preseason with a 1–2 victory over [[MLS Cup 2014|Major League Soccer champions]] [[LA Galaxy]] in the [[2015 International Champions Cup]]. Goals from [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]] and [[Sergi Roberto]] secured the win in front of a crowd of 93,226 at the [[Rose Bowl (stadium)|Rose Bowl]] in [[Pasadena, California]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/international-champions-cup/round-1-a/fc-barcelona_los-angeles-galaxy |title=Barça kick-off with victory. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=22 July 2015 |access-date=23 July 2015}}</ref> On 23 July, Barcelona were fined €30,000 by [[UEFA]] for fans waving [[Catalan independence|pro-Catalan independence banners]] at the [[2015 UEFA Champions League Final]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/jul/23/barcelona-fined-uefa-pro-catalan-banners-champions-league |title=Barça fined for pro-Catalan flags at Berlin Final. |work=The Guardian|date=23 July 2015 |access-date=24 July 2015}}</ref> The club maintains its respect for the sanction, yet does not agree with it and its legal services will consider the possibility of questioning the fine at a later time.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/club/detail/article/fc-barcelona-press-release-on-the-uefa-sanction |title=Barça statements on fines. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=23 July 2015 |access-date=24 July 2015}}</ref> On 25 July, Barcelona were defeated by English side [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] with a scoreline of 1–3 at [[Levi's Stadium]] in [[Santa Clara, California]]. The lone goal came from [[Rafinha (footballer, born February 1993)|Rafinha]] in the 89th minute of play.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/international-champions-cup/round-2-a/fc-barcelona_manchester-u |title=Barça first defeat of summer. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=26 July 2015 |access-date=27 July 2015}}</ref> On 28 July, Barcelona were defeated in penalties by [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] at [[FedExField]] in [[Landover, Maryland]]. Goals from Luis Suárez and [[Sandro Ramírez|Sandro]] were enough to earn the regular time draw, however the team lost in penalties 4–2 to end their United States Summer Tour.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/international-champions-cup/round-3-a/chelsea_fc-barcelona |title=Barça lose on penalties. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=29 July 2015 |access-date=29 July 2015}}</ref>

===August===
On 2 August, Barcelona finished their pre-season tour with a visit to [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] at the [[Stadio Artemio Franchi]] in [[Florence]]. The match ended with a 2–1 loss to the Catalans, the lone Barça goal coming from Luis Suárez.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/international-champions-cup/round-4-a/fiorentina_fc-barcelona |title=Barça lose to Fiorentina. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=2 August 2015 |access-date=3 August 2015}}</ref> Three days later, on 5 August, Barcelona took on Italian club [[A.S. Roma|Roma]] in the 50th edition of the annual [[Joan Gamper Trophy]]. The game ended 3–0 to the Catalan club with goals coming from [[Neymar]], [[Lionel Messi]] and [[Ivan Rakitić]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/happy-gamper-for-fc-barcelona-against-roma-3-0 |title=Barça take the Gamper. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=5 August 2015 |access-date=8 August 2015}}</ref> As a result of winning the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League]] the previous season, the team was eligible to compete in the [[2015 UEFA Super Cup]] versus [[2014–15 UEFA Europa League]] winner Sevilla. The game took place on 11 August at the [[Boris Paichadze Dinamo Arena]] in [[Tbilisi]], [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]], and ended 5–4 in favour of Barcelona, with a brace from Messi and [[Pedro (footballer, born July 1987)|Pedro]] scoring the winner in extra time.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/european-supercup/final/fc-barcelona_sevilla-fc |title=Fourth title of 2015. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=11 August 2015 |access-date=12 August 2015}}</ref> With the win, Barcelona becomes the [[FC Barcelona in European football|club with the most international trophies]] in Europe with 19 international titles.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-top-uefa-ranking-for-international-titles |title=Barça goes on top with most international titles. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=13 August 2015 |access-date=13 August 2015}}</ref>

On 12 August, UEFA announced Messi, Suárez and [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]]'s [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] as the finalists for the [[UEFA Best Player in Europe Award|2014–15 UEFA Best Player in Europe Award]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-s-messi-and-suarez-and-real-madrid-s-ronaldo-finalists-for-2014-15-uefa-best-player-in-europe-award |title=UEFA Player of the year include two from Barça. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=12 August 2015 |access-date=13 August 2015}}</ref> On 14 August, Barcelona were soundly defeated by [[Athletic Bilbao]] 4–0 in the first leg of the [[2015 Supercopa de España]] at the [[San Mamés Stadium (2013)|San Mamés Stadium]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/supercopa-spanyol/final-1st-leg/athletic-club_fc-barcelona |title=First leg goes to Athletic. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=14 August 2015 |access-date=24 August 2015}}</ref> On 17 August, Barcelona failed to win their second trophy of the season after a 1–1 draw in the second leg of 2015 Supercopa de España. The lone goal from Messi was not enough to overturn a four-goal deficit from the first leg.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/supercopa-spanyol/final-2nd-leg/fc-barcelona_athletic-club |title=Barça's bid for six trophies ends at Spanish Supercup. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=18 August 2015 |access-date=24 August 2015}}</ref>

On 20 August, Pedro joined [[2014–15 Premier League|Premier League champions]] Chelsea for €27&nbsp;million, rising to €30&nbsp;million on variables, ending his 11-year association with Barcelona.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2015/08/pedro-signs-for-chelsea-.html |title=Pedro signs for Chelsea. |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |date=20 August 2015 |access-date=20 August 2015}}</ref> On 23 August, Barcelona kicked off the [[2015–16 La Liga]] season with a 0–1 victory over Athletic Bilbao in [[Bilbao]]. This was the third meeting between the two teams in the last nine days that included the two legs of the 2015 Supercopa de España. On 27 August, Barcelona were drawn into [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League group stage#Group E|Group E]] of the [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League]] with [[Bundesliga]] side [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]], Roma and [[2014 Belarusian Premier League|Belarusian champions]] [[FC BATE Borisov|BATE Borisov]]. At the same event, Messi was crowned the 2014–15 UEFA Best Player in Europe for the second time in his career.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/0253-0d8010f4daf5-96e9bd17274b-1000--messi-named-best-player-in-europe-for-second-time/ |title=Messi 2014-15 Best Player in Europe. |publisher=UEFA |date=27 August 2015 |access-date=27 August 2015}}</ref> On 29 August, Barcelona played their first match at home against [[Málaga CF|Málaga]] which ended in a 1–0 victory. [[Thomas Vermaelen]] scored the only and his first goal for the club.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/league/round-2/fc-barcelona_malaga-cf/report |title=Barça notch first home win. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=30 August 2015 |access-date=9 September 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150831172117/http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/league/round-2/fc-barcelona_malaga-cf/report |archive-date=31 August 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===September===
On 1 September, Barcelona and English side [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] agreed on the loan of [[Alex Song]] for a second successive season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/song |title=Song loaned back to West Ham. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=1 September 2015 |access-date=9 September 2015}}</ref> On 13 September, Barcelona traveled to the [[Vicente Calderón Stadium]] to face Atlético Madrid after the FIFA international break. The host took the lead with a goal from [[Fernando Torres]], but goals from [[Neymar]] and substitute Messi completed the comeback and notched a 1–2 victory. Barcelona goalkeeper [[Marc-André ter Stegen]] made his La Liga debut after only appearing in the Champions League and [[Copa del Rey]] last season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/atletico-de-madrid-v-fc-barcelona-comeback-victory-at-the-calderon-21 |title=Comeback victory at the Calderón. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=12 September 2015 |access-date=13 September 2015}}</ref> On 16 September, Barcelona open their European campaign with a 1–1 draw against Roma at the [[Stadio Olimpico]], with the goal coming from Luis Suárez in the first half.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/champions-league/round-1-e/roma_fc-barcelona |title=Draw to begin European quest. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=16 September 2015 |access-date=17 September 2015}}</ref> The match ended on a sour note for the squad after Rafinha left the pitch on a stretcher with a leg injury after a tackle from Roma midfielder [[Radja Nainggolan]]. The next day, the team released a statement that the player had tear the right [[anterior cruciate ligament]] (ACL) and is likely to miss the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-midfielder-rafinha-tears-right-acl |title=Rafinha tears ACL. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=16 September 2015 |access-date=17 September 2015}}</ref>

On 20 September, Barcelona defeated [[UD Levante|Levante]] at home by a 4–1 scoreline with a brace from Messi to stay undefeated in league.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-v-levante-catalans-ride-second-half-surge-to-41-victory-stay-perfect-in-la-liga |title=Barça win over Levante. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=20 September 2015 |access-date=30 September 2015}}</ref> Three days later in [[Balaídos]] in [[Vigo]], Barça were soundly defeated 4–1 by [[Celta de Vigo]] to suffer their first league defeat and drop out of first place in the table.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/rc-celta-de-vigo-v-fc-barcelona-beaten-at-balaidos-4-1 |title=Barça pummeled at Vigo. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=23 September 2015 |access-date=30 September 2015}}</ref> On 26 September, Barcelona were able to bounce back at home with a 2–1 victory over [[2014–15 Segunda División#League table|newly promoted]] [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/league/round-6/fc-barcelona_ud-las-palmas |title=Barcelona victory over Las Palmas. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=27 September 2015 |access-date=30 September 2015}}</ref> The match was marred with the costly injury to Messi, who suffered a tear in the [[medial collateral ligament]] (MCL) of his [[Knee|left knee]]. The injury will keep the star player out for approximately 6–8 weeks.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/leo-messi-out-for-seven-to-eight-weeks |title=Messi out 6-8 weeks with injury. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=26 September 2015 |access-date=30 September 2015}}</ref>

On 29 September, Barcelona defeated Bayer Leverkusen in come from behind fashion with a 2–1 victory. The visitors took the lead in the 22nd minute with a [[corner kick]] goal from [[Defender (association football)|defender]] [[Kyriakos Papadopoulos]]. In the 80th minute, [[Sergi Roberto]] leveled the score and two minutes later, Suárez completed the comeback to keep Barça at the top of [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League group stage#Group E|Group E]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/champions-league/round-2-e/fc-barcelona_bayer-leverkusen |title=Barcelona earn comeback victory. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=29 September 2015 |access-date=30 September 2015}}</ref> For the second straight Champions League match, Barça lose a key player to injury. This time, [[Captain (association football)|captain]] [[Andrés Iniesta]] went down with a [[hamstring]] injury in his [[Human leg|right leg]] that will keep him out 3–4 weeks.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.es/futbol/primer-equipo/detalle/noticia/iniesta-sufre-una-lesion-en-el-biceps-femoral-de-la-pierna-derecha |title=Iniesta goes down with injury. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=29 September 2015 |access-date=30 September 2015}}</ref>

===October===
On 3 October, Barcelona was defeated by Sevilla 2–1 away at the [[Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán Stadium]] for the club's second loss in last three league games. Neymar scored from a second-half penalty kick<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/league/round-7/sevilla-fc_fc-barcelona |title=Sevilla FC v FC Barcelona: Late rally comes up short in 2–1 defeat |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=3 October 2015 |access-date=3 October 2015}}</ref> as [[Unai Emery]] beat Barcelona for first ever time as a manager.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sport-english.com/en/news/liga-bbva/unai-emery-beats-barcelona-for-first-ever-time-manager-4559911 |title=Unai Emery beats Barcelona for first ever time as a manager |work=Sport|location=Spain |date=3 October 2015 |access-date=3 October 2015}}</ref>

===November===
On 21 November, Barcelona thrashed Real Madrid 0–4 in the season's first ''[[El Clásico|Clásico]]'', played at the [[Santiago Bernabeu Stadium]]. Luis Suárez scored a brace while Neymar and Andrés Iniesta also got in the scoresheet; later, Lionel Messi played his first match as a substitute after recovering from his two-month injury.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/league/round-12/reial-madrid-cf_fc-barcelona |title= Barça run to El Clásico rout at the Bernabéu |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=22 November 2015 |access-date=22 November 2015}}</ref> On 24 November, Barcelona beat Roma 6–1 in the Champions League and secured top spot in Group E.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/champions-league/round-5-e/fc-barcelona_roma |title= FC Barcelona hit Roma for six (6-1) |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=24 November 2015 |access-date=24 November 2015}}</ref>

===December===
On 14 December, in the draw for the round of 16 of Champions League, Barcelona will face [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] as the Group E winner.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0253-0d0451cd01d9-a249efb8e43f-1000--round-of-16-draw-arsenal-v-barca-juve-v-bayern/|title=Round of 16 draw: Arsenal v Barça, Juve v Bayern|date=14 December 2015|publisher=UEFA}}</ref> On 20 December, the club won a record third [[FIFA Club World Cup]] title after defeating Argentine side [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]] 3–0 in the [[2015 FIFA Club World Cup#Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/clubworldcup/news/y=2015/m=12/news=barcelona-secure-historic-third-title-in-japan-2747220.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151223105706/http://www.fifa.com/clubworldcup/news/y=2015/m=12/news=barcelona-secure-historic-third-title-in-japan-2747220.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=23 December 2015 |title=Barcelona secure historic third title in Japan |publisher=FIFA |date=20 December 2015 |access-date=20 December 2015}}</ref> Luis Suárez scored a record five goals in the tournament including two goals in the [[2015 FIFA Club World Cup Final|final]] and a hat trick in the [[2015 FIFA Club World Cup#Semi-finals|semi-final]]. He was awarded the Adidas Golden ball, given to the best player of the tournament.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/clubworldcup/news/y=2015/m=12/news=barcelona-trio-raumt-ab-2747108-2747184.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151220152446/http://www.fifa.com/clubworldcup/news/y=2015/m=12/news=barcelona-trio-raumt-ab-2747108-2747184.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=20 December 2015 |title=Barcelona trio sweep awards |publisher=FIFA |date=20 December 2015 |access-date=20 December 2015}}</ref>

On 30 December, Barcelona beat [[Real Betis]] 4–0, with Suárez netting a second-half double after Lionel Messi, in his 500th game, scored; Betis also scored an own goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/league/round-17/fc-barcelona_real-betis-balompie|title=FC Barcelona claim 4–0 victory over Betis and top spot to end 2015|date=31 December 2015|publisher=FC Barcelona}}</ref> By scoring 180 goals in 2015 in all competitions, Barcelona set the record for most goals scored in a calendar year, breaking Real Madrid's record of 178 goals scored in 2014.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/180-goals-and-51-wins-in-a-record-breaking-2015|title=180 Goals and 51 Wins in a record breaking 2015|date=31 December 2015|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=20 February 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160104165240/http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/180-goals-and-51-wins-in-a-record-breaking-2015|archive-date=4 January 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===January===
On 11 January 2016, Messi won the [[2015 FIFA Ballon d'Or|FIFA Ballon d'Or]] for a record fifth time in his career.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/ballon-dor/news/y=2016/m=1/news=messi-this-is-for-those-who-wish-me-well-2755196.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160114033457/http://www.fifa.com/ballon-dor/news/y=2016/m=1/news=messi-this-is-for-those-who-wish-me-well-2755196.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=14 January 2016|title=Messi: This is for those who wish me well|publisher=FIFA|date=11 January 2016}}</ref> Luis Enrique's Barcelona has finished a January with nearly perfect statistics. Just the draw against [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] at the [[RCDE Stadium|Cornellà-El Prat]] in the first game of the year has held them back in 2016.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sport-english.com/en/news/barca/barcelona-make-best-league-start-since-pep-guardiola-2009-4860153 |title=Barcelona make best January start since Pep Guardiola in 2009 |work=Sport|location=Spain |date=31 January 2016 |access-date=31 January 2016}}</ref>

===February===
On 10 February, Barcelona's Copa del Rey draw with [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] saw Luis Enrique's side set a new club record for unbeaten games, beating [[Pep Guardiola]]'s 2011 vintage with their 29th game without a loss.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/fc-barcelona/20160210/302066103178/record-historico-del-barca-de-lucho-29-partidos-seguidos-sin-perder.html |title=Récord histórico del Barça de Lucho: 29 partidos seguidos sin perder |publisher=mundodeportivo.com |date=10 February 2016 |access-date=10 February 2016}}</ref> On 17 February, Messi made more history after scoring his 300th and 301st goal in La Liga, becoming the first player ever to do so.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sport-english.com/en/news/barca/leo-messi-hits-300th-liga-goal-against-sporting-gijon-4906157 |title=Leo Messi hits 300th La Liga goal against Sporting Gijon |work=Sport|location=Spain |date=17 February 2016 |access-date=17 February 2016}}</ref> In the same match, Luis Suárez made up for a penalty miss with his 24th league goal of the season as Barça beat [[Sporting de Gijón]] 3–1.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/league/round-16/sporting-de-gijon_fc-barcelona |title=Sporting Gijón v FC Barcelona: A win worth waiting for (1-3) |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=17 February 2016 |access-date=17 February 2016}}</ref> On 23 February, Barcelona defeated Arsenal 0–2 away in [[London]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/arsenal-fc-v-fc-barcelona-premier-victory-in-london-0-2 |title=Arsenal FC v FC Barcelona: Premier victory in London (0-2) |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=24 February 2016 |access-date=24 February 2016}}</ref> with Messi scoring twice in a feverishly paced encounter, including the 10,000th goal scored in club history.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/barca-reach-10-000-goals-in-official-competition |title=Barça reach 10,000 goals in official competition |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=24 February 2016 |access-date=24 February 2016}}</ref> On 25 February, Barcelona extend their alliance with [[UNICEF]] through to 2020; the club will increase its annual donation to the charity from €1.5&nbsp;million to €2&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://foundation.fcbarcelona.com/detail/article/fc-barcelona-and-unicef-renew-and-strengthen-their-alliance |title=FC Barcelona and UNICEF renew and strengthen their alliance |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=25 February 2016 |access-date=25 February 2016 |archive-date=26 February 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160226102550/http://foundation.fcbarcelona.com/detail/article/fc-barcelona-and-unicef-renew-and-strengthen-their-alliance |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===March===
On 3 March, Barcelona defeated [[Rayo Vallecano]] away 1–5, with [[Ivan Rakitić]] and Arda Turan netting one each and Messi scoring a hat-trick.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/league/round-27/rayo-vallecano_fc-barcelona |title=Rayo Vallecano v FC Barcelona: Unbeatably brilliant (1-5) |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=4 March 2016 |access-date=4 March 2016}}</ref> Barça set an all-time record run for 35 games unbeaten in Spanish football, previously held by Real Madrid's 1988–89 side managed by Dutchman [[Leo Beenhakker]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/a-new-record-35-games-unbeaten |title=A new record: 35 games unbeaten |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=4 March 2016 |access-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304023008/http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/a-new-record-35-games-unbeaten |archive-date=4 March 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On 8 March, the club announced that the Espai Barça<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/club/detail/article/new-espai-barca-explained |title=New Espai Barça explained |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=3 February 2014 |access-date=8 March 2016}}</ref> jury unanimously selected the bid by [[Nikken Sekkei]] + Pascual i Ausió Arquitectes as the winner of the tender for the design of the new Camp Nou.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/club/detail/article/espai-barca-jury-selects-proposal-from-nikken-sekkei-pascual-i-ausio-arquitectes-team-for-the-new-camp-nou |title=This is the New Camp Nou |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=8 March 2016 |access-date=8 March 2016}}</ref>

On 16 March, Barça defeated Arsenal 3–1 at home (5–1 aggregate) in the round of 16 of the Champions League to gain access to the competition's quarter-finals for the ninth-straight season,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/champions-league/1-8-2nd-leg/fc-barcelona_arsenal |title=FC Barcelona v Arsenal: A quarter to nine |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=16 March 2016 |access-date=16 March 2016}}</ref> and set a new club record for ten consecutive Champions League wins at Camp Nou.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.barcafan-club.com/2016/03/fc-barcelona-set-record-ten-consecutive-champions-league-wins-at-camp-nou/ |title=FC Barcelona set record ten consecutive Champions League wins at Camp Nou |publisher=barcafan-club.com |date=17 March 2016}}</ref> On 18 March, in the draw for the quarter-finals of Champions League, Barcelona will face Atlético Madrid.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/022b-0e93c06311a3-0e2c9ebe3c93-1000--quarter-final-draw-barcelona-atletico-paris-city/|title=Quarter-final draw: Barcelona-Atlético, Paris-City|date=18 March 2016|publisher=UEFA}}</ref> On 24 March, legendary Barcelona player and coach [[Johan Cruyff]] died of illness at 68, surrounded by his family in [[Barcelona]];<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2016/mar/24/johan-cruyff-dies-aged-68-holland-football-legend|title=Johan Cruyff, Dutch football legend, dies at the age of 68|date=24 March 2016|work=The Guardian|access-date=24 March 2016}}</ref> the club mourned him with flags at Camp Nou placed at [[half-mast]].<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.fcbarcelona.com/club/detail/article/fc-barcelona-mourns-the-death-of-johan-cruyff |title=FC Barcelona mourns the death of Johan Cruyff|date=24 March 2016|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=24 March 2016}}</ref>

===April===
On 2 April, Real Madrid won the second ''El Clásico'' match of the league season with a 1–2 victory away, breaking Barcelona's unbeaten record at 39 matches.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/league/round-31/fc-barcelona_reial-madrid-cf |title=FC Barcelona fall to Real Madrid, 2–1, as long unbeaten streak ends in disappointment |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=2 April 2016 |access-date=2 April 2016}}</ref> Players, directors and supporters remembered Johan Cruyff in the form of a video, a mosaic, a minute's silence and applause before the game.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/johan-cruyff-honoured-on-an-emotional-evening-at-the-camp-nou |title=Johan Cruyff honoured on an emotional evening at the Camp Nou |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=2 April 2016 |access-date=2 April 2016}}</ref> On 5 April, Barcelona defeated Atlético Madrid at home (2–1) in the first leg of their Champions League draw, after Luis Suárez's two goals in the second half reversed Barça's early one-goal deficit.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/champions-league/1-4-1st-leg/fc-barcelona_atletic-de-madrid |title=FC Barcelona take first-leg thriller in 2–1 victory over Atlético Madrid |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=5 April 2016 |access-date=5 April 2016}}</ref>

Barcelona lost 1–0 away at the [[Anoeta Stadium]] to [[Real Sociedad]] on 9 April in La Liga after a goal from the latter club early on.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/league/round-32/reial-societat_fc-barcelona |title=Real Sociedad v FC Barcelona: Agony at Anoeta (1-0) |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=9 April 2016 |access-date=9 April 2016}}</ref> On 13 April, Atlético defeated Barcelona 2–0 (3–2 on aggregate) in the second leg of the Champions League quarter-finals, eliminating the title holders.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/champions-league/1-4-2nd-leg/atletic-de-madrid_fc-barcelona |title=Atlético Madrid v FC Barcelona: Goodbye to the Champions League... Now the league and Copa del Rey (2-0) |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=13 April 2016 |access-date=13 April 2016}}</ref> On 17 April, Barcelona suffered their third consecutive loss of the competition as they were out-played by Valencia in a 1–2 home defeat,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/league/round-33/fc-barcelona_valencia-cf |title=FC Barcelona down but not out after falling to Valencia, 2–1 |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=17 April 2016 |access-date=17 April 2016}}</ref> despite Messi's second-half goal, his 450th for the club.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/messi-reaches-450-goals-for-fc-barcelona |title=Messi reaches 450 goals for FC Barcelona |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=17 April 2016 |access-date=17 April 2016}}</ref>

On 20 April, Barcelona shook off their recent poor form to absolutely thump [[Deportivo de La Coruña]] in a 0–8 away victory, with Luis Suárez scoring four and creating three assists to keep his side in the title race.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/deportivo-la-coruna-v-fc-barcelona-thats-more-like-it |title=Deportivo La Coruña 0-8 FC Barcelona: That's more like it! |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=20 April 2016 |access-date=20 April 2016}}</ref> They continued this form three days later by beating Sporting de Gijón 6–0, with Suárez again scoring four goals (two from penalties), with Messi and Neymar scoring the other two.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/league/round-35/fc-barcelona_sporting-de-gijon |title=Love set for FC Barcelona in 6–0 shutout of Sporting de Gijón |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=23 April 2016 |access-date=23 April 2016}}</ref> On 30 April, Barcelona defeated Real Betis 0–2 through Ivan Rakitić and Suárez goals, keeping Barça top of La Liga.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/league/round-36/real-betis-balompie_fc-barcelona |title=Real Betis v FC Barcelona: One step closer (0-2) |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=30 April 2016 |access-date=30 April 2016}}</ref>

===May===
On 8 May, Barcelona thrashed Espanyol 5–0 in the season's last home match.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/league/round-37/fc-barcelona_rcd-espanyol |title=FC Barcelona v RCD Espanyol: One game away |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=8 May 2016 |access-date=8 May 2016}}</ref> Everyone inside Camp Nou played their part in the spectacular pre-game mosaic which bore the message "''Som-hi tots''" ("Let's go everyone") and also in the minute's silence in memory of the recently passed Manel Vich, the voice of Camp Nou for almost 60 years.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/the-best-crowd-for-the-derby-against-espanyol-in-the-last-10-years |title=The best crowd for the derby against Espanyol in the last 10 years |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=8 May 2016 |access-date=8 May 2016}}</ref> On 14 May 2016, Barcelona sealed their sixth La Liga title in eight years with an emphatic 0–3 win over [[Granada CF|Granada]]. Two strikes from Luis Suárez in the first half and another late in the second helped the Catalans achieve the club's 24th league success, and confirms the Uruguayan's status as the division's top marksman with 40 goals.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/granada-v-fc-barcelona-catalans-cruise-to-la-liga-title-0-3 |title=Granada v FC Barcelona: Barça claim La Liga title (0-3) |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=14 May 2016 |access-date=14 May 2016}}</ref>

On 21 May, Barcelona and [[Nike Inc.|Nike]] extended their current sponsorship deal.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/club/detail/article/nike-and-fc-barcelona-extend-their-agreement |title=Barça and NIKE extend their agreement |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=21 May 2016 |access-date=21 May 2016}}</ref> On 22 May, Barcelona recorded a 2–0 extra time victory over Sevilla for their second domestic title of the season and 28th Copa del Rey of all-time.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-v-sevilla-fc-double-the-pleasure-2-0-copa-del-rey-final |title=FC Barcelona v Sevilla FC: Double the pleasure! (2–0) |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=23 May 2016 |access-date=23 May 2016}}</ref> On 27 May, Barcelona and [[Sergio Busquets]] are set to renew his contract for five seasons, through to 30 June 2021.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/sergio-busquets-extends-contract-with-fc-barcelona |title=Sergio Busquets to extend contract with FC Barcelona |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=27 May 2016 |access-date=27 May 2016}}</ref>

=== Origin ===

Josep Maria Bartomeu reviewed his time in office before an audience of about 250 club directors, commission members, guests, members and supporters of the club's peñas at the Auditori 1899. The board was to resign at an extraordinary meeting so that a caretaker commission could call elections. The commission was to be chaired by Ramon Adell, president of the club's economic commission, and include the commission's other members, the Síndic del Soci Joan Manuel Trayter, outgoing economic vice president Javier Faus, and two further board members.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/fc-barcelona/20150609/20406153818/bartomeu-defiende-su-gestion-y-reclama-una-campana-modelica.html |title=Bartomeu defiende su gestión y reclama “una campaña modélica” |access-date=27 August 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sport.es/es/noticias/barca/bartomeu-somos-mejor-club-del-mundo-tenemos-mejor-equipo-del-mundo-4260003 |title=Bartomeu: "Somos el mejor club del mundo y tenemos el mejor equipo del mundo" |access-date=27 August 2026}}</ref>
